assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Low-double-digit EV/EBITDA for large-cap pharma is my prior, not a fact in this run's evidence — treat it as a proposal for verification against a peer set. What the evidence does support: EBIT margin rising 2.8% to 23.4%, D&A of ~11.5% of revenue (largely Alexion-era amortisation) making EBITDA margin far above EBIT, and genuine franchise diversification. I discounted from a growth rating because the derivation holds 11.9% revenue growth flat, likely overstating terminal EBITDA. Of the two, I prefer the exit multiple as the terminal value estimate: the discount rate is undetermined, and a perpetuity would capitalise a D&A-over-capex wedge (11.5% vs 3.3% of revenue) that cannot persist for ever.

Grounded in the evidence of a five-therapy-area, four-region portfolio with no single-blockbuster dependence and active Phase III readouts — that supports growth continuing, but perpetual loss-of-exclusivity erosion and payer price pressure prevent a pharma major compounding above nominal GDP for ever. Raise toward 0.03 if pipeline replacement is judged durable; cut toward 0.02 if US pricing policy or the Forxiga patent proceedings are expected to bite.
